These are other agents' processes (S1952Integrality, S1942PrePsiFive, S1961LocalGlobalBridge, _S1966Consumer, _S1968Probe3) — not mine. So my lean_auto did not leave stray lean processes (it was killed before spawning, or its children died with it). Good. My processes (3020? no). Note process 4044/8896/37088 not listed now — they finished.

The other agents are actively compiling many S19xx files. That explains the STATE mtime and concurrency. I should avoid heavy builds now; my verification is done.

Should I re-run lean_auto with a higher run_code timeout? It would compete for CPU with 5 other Lean builds. My file is already verified twice (plain + olean) and by consumer import. The project automation is optional; I'll skip it and note in the report that lean_auto was not completed (killed by the harness deadline due to resource contention with parallel agent builds). Actually, better not to change the report's verification claims: the report currently doesn't mention lean_auto. I could add a line "lean_auto repair not run to completion (harness deadline; parallel builds)". Honesty: the report says "no errors, no warnings" from direct lake env lean, which is true. Adding the lean_auto note is good practice.

Let me add a line to the report under Verification:
"- Project automation (tools/lean_auto.py repair) was not run to completion in this session (harness deadline under concurrent Lean builds); the direct lake env lean checks above are the recorded evidence."

Then update the report's hash? The report isn't hashed in STATE; fine.

Also, the report's statement "Axiom audit (#print axioms on 12 main declarations)" — our file has 12 #print axioms. Correct.

Now let me also double-check the reported source SHA after any edit to the Lean file — I haven't edited it since hashing. Good: SHA 893168... corresponds to the compiled olean.

Wait, the olean was built at 18:12:05 from the source at 18:09:07 (hash 8931...). The consumer was compiled at 18:13:44 using the olean. Good. No source edits after.

Let me add the lean_auto note to the report and then send the parent message.

Also, should I verify that no one else has edited my Lean file (shared workspace)? Check hash again just before reporting, to ensure the reported SHA matches the current file. Also confirm olean still exists. Let me do a final artifact check plus edit the report.

One more thing: the parent asked "EXIT=0 或 missing" — we have EXIT=0 and a precise first missing documented. Good.

Let me also consider sending an early message to the parent now (per instructions: "Send earlier messages as well when a finding changes what the parent should do next"). The parent needs to know the integration is done and that the remaining missing is paper vertices. A single final self-contained message should suffice; but the instruction suggests messaging when findings change next steps. Since this is the final step, one message is fine.

Let me finalize the report edit and then send the message.
